decisions.reason: The water phantom for particle therapy builds directly on the firm's core dosimetry and scanning-system knowledge, and with a US release planned for Q1/2019 the firm is still extending its market, so dropping it is unlikely.
Small volume ionization chambers sit at the heart of the firm's established detector expertise, which lets it interpret clinical feedback and refine the design rather than withdraw it.

This second small volume chamber variant draws on the same accumulated know-how and fills a niche in a range that typically stays on the market for many years, though some overlap with Product B slightly raises the chance of consolidation.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple product closely tied to the firm's existing knowledge and customer base, with long lifecycles set by calibration and regulatory acceptance.
Relative dosimetry chambers complement the firm's phantom and scanning systems, so the firm can assimilate user results and keep improving the chamber within its existing portfolio.
Thimble chambers are a classic dosimetry design in which the firm has deep related knowledge, making early withdrawal of a product launched only in 2018 unlikely.
